Let me analyze this OIML certificate carefully.

Certificate details:
- Number: R49/2013-SK1-16.03
- Member State: Slovakia
- Date issued: 8 March 2016 → 2016-03-08
- Scheme: not explicitly stated (this is OIML-CS, likely scheme A but not stated — don't fabricate)
- Page total: 5 pages
- Project number: not mentioned

Issuing Authority:
- Name: Slovak Legal Metrology
- Address: Hviezdoslavova 31, 974 01 Banská Bystrica, Slovakia
- Person responsible: Jaromír Markovič
- Title: Ing. Jaromír Markovič, PhD.

Applicant:
- Name: Ningbo Aimei Meter Manufacture Co., Ltd.
- Address: 68, West Town Road, Shangtian Town, Fenghua City, Zhejiang, 315511 P.R. of China

Manufacturer: "The applicant" — so same as applicant. I could add manufacturers[] entry with the same name, or note that the manufacturer is the applicant. I'll include the manufacturer as the applicant company since "The applicant".

Certified type:
- Category: Water meter (the schema examples list "Gas meter" etc.; water meter fits — "Mechanical single-jet dry dial water meter type for metering of cold water"). I'll use "Water meter".
- Type designations: SD-A, SD-AP
- Description: text from pages 2

Recommendation:
- R 49-1, edition 2013, accuracy class 2. Canonical ID: "R49" with edition 2013? The recommendation is R 49-1 (part 1). The canonical id would be "R49". Edition 2013. Amendment: none. Accuracy classes: [2]. Scheme: not stated.

Actually the certificate references R 49-1, R 49-2, R 49-3. The main recommendation for the certificate is R 49-1 edition 2013. I'll put id "R49", edition 2013, accuracy_classes ["2"] or [2]. The schema says accuracy_classes[] — I'll use [2] as number? Probably strings. Let me use ["2"]? Examples don't show. Accuracy class 2 — I'll use [2] as number. Hmm, safer: ["2"]? For water meters, class 2. I'll use [2].

Test reports:
- No. 2015/CV009/312.03, 59 pages, role: type_evaluation_report (it's the associated OIML Test Report). Role options: type_evaluation_report | test_report | documentation_file | evaluation_report. The test report is the OIML Test Report → "test_report". Date not given. Pages: 59.

Documentation: Manufacturer's technical documentation stored in folder Aimei_SD_A_00 — that's a documentation file. Could add as test_reports[] with role "documentation_file": id "Aimei_SD_A_00". Yes, section 7 says "Documentation used for assessment purposes": Test report No 2015/CV009/312.03; Manufacturer's technical documentation stored in folder Aimei_SD_A_00. I'll add both.

Model family: The cert covers two types SD-A and SD-AP. Then the table shows DN 15 and DN 20, with different flow rates. Actually it's a matrix: DN (15, 20) × installation orientation (H, V) × ratio R (80, 100, 125, 160 for H; 40 for V).

Let me parse the tables carefully.

Table 1 (page 3):
- Type SD-A / SD-AP
- Nominal diameter DN: 15 | 20
- Connection thread: G ¾ B (for DN15) | G 1B (for DN20)
- Construction length L: 110/115/130/165 (DN15) | 130/165/190 (DN20) mm
- Water temperature range ϑ: T30, T50 (°C)
- Maximum working pressure: 16 bar
- MPE upper: ±2 (at ϑ ≤ 30°C), ±3 (at ϑ>30°C) %
- MPE lower: ±5 %
- Scale interval: 0,000 05 m³ → 0.00005 m³
- Capacity of calculator: 9999,99995 m³ → 9999.99995 m³
- Mechanical class: M1
- Climatic class: -10 to +55 °C
- Installation orientation: H

Then second block in Table 1:
- DN 15 | 20
- Permanent flowrate Q₃: 2,5 | 4 m³/h
- Minimum flowrate Q₁: 0,03125 | 0,025 | 0,02 | 0,015625 | 0,05 | 0,04 | 0,032 | 0,025 m³/h
- Transitional flowrate Q₂: 0,05 | 0,04 | 0,032 | 0,025 | 0,08 | 0,064 | 0,0512 | 0,04 m³/h
- Overload flowrate Q₄: 3,125 | 5 m³/h
- Ratio Q₃/Q₁: 80 | 100 | 125 | 160 | 80 | 100 | 125 | 160 R

So for H orientation:
- DN15, Q3=2.5: four variants with R = 80 (Q1=0.03125, Q2=0.05), 100 (Q1=0.025, Q2=0.04), 125 (Q1=0.02, Q2=0.032), 160 (Q1=0.015625, Q2=0.025)
- DN20, Q3=4: R=80 (Q1=0.05, Q2=0.08), 100 (Q1=0.04, Q2=0.064), 125 (Q1=0.032, Q2=0.0512), 160 (Q1=0.025, Q2=0.04)
- Q4: 3.125 (DN15), 5 (DN20)

Second table (page 4): V orientation:
- Ratio Q₂/Q₁: 1,6
- Installation orientation: V
- DN: 15 | 20
- Q3: 2,5 | 4
- Q1: 0,0625 | 0,1
- Q2: 0,1 | 0,16
- Q4: 3,125 | 5
- Ratio Q₃/Q₁: 40
- Ratio Q₂/Q₁: 1,6

Footnote: *) horizontal position with the indication device positioned at the top only — this relates to the H orientation row (highlighted cell).

So the model matrix: 2 types (SD-A, SD-AP) × 2 DN (15, 20) × orientation (H, V) × R values. The type SD-A vs SD-AP differ only in body material (brass vs plastic). The types and DN and orientation and ratio create variants.

How to model? Options:
1. model_family.models with model_id like "SD-A;DN15;H;R80" etc. That could be 2×2×... too many: H orientation: DN15 has 4 R values, DN20 has 4 R values → 8; V: 2 (one per DN). Total 10 per type → 20 total. That's a lot.

Alternatively use config_level with axes: DN, orientation, ratio Q3/Q1. The schema says config_level is for attribute × config-axis matrices. This fits well: characteristics vary by DN and orientation axes.

Let me use model_family.models for the two types (SD-A, SD-AP) — actually they're types, listed in type_designations. Hmm. The model_family should include only if cert covers >1 model variant. It covers SD-A and SD-AP plus DN variants. I think model_family with models = the configuration variants could be reasonable, but 20 entries is heavy.

Alternative approach: use config_level entries:
- attribute: permanent_flowrate_q3, axis: nominal_diameter, values: [{condition: "DN 15", value: 2.5, unit: m³/h}, {condition: "DN 20", value: 4}]
- attribute: minimum_flowrate_q1, axis: "nominal_diameter × orientation × ratio_q3_over_q1", values: many conditions.

That's 16 Q1 values for H (8 DN15? no — 4 for DN15, 4 for DN20) plus 2 for V. Total 10 values.

Let me structure config_level:

1. attribute: minimum_flowrate_q1, axis: "nominal_diameter|installation_orientation|ratio_q3_q1", values:
   - {condition: "DN=15, orientation=H, ratio=80", value: 0.03125, unit: "m³/h"}
   - {condition: "DN=15, orientation=H, ratio=100", value: 0.025}
   - {condition: "DN=15, orientation=H, ratio=125", value: 0.02}
   - {condition: "DN=15, orientation=H, ratio=160", value: 0.015625}
   - {condition: "DN=20, orientation=H, ratio=80", value: 0.05}
   - {condition: "DN=20, orientation=H, ratio=100", value: 0.04}
   - {condition: "DN=20, orientation=H, ratio=125", value: 0.032}
   - {condition: "DN=20, orientation=H, ratio=160", value: 0.025}
   - {condition: "DN=15, orientation=V, ratio=40", value: 0.0625}
   - {condition: "DN=20, orientation=V, ratio=40", value: 0.1}

2. Same for transitional_flowrate_q2:
   - DN15 H: 0.05, 0.04, 0.032, 0.025
   - DN20 H: 0.08, 0.064, 0.0512, 0.04
   - DN15 V: 0.1
   - DN20 V: 0.16

3. permanent_flowrate_q3 axis nominal_diameter: DN15 → 2.5, DN20 → 4
4. overload_flowrate_q4 axis nominal_diameter: DN15 → 3.125, DN20 → 5
5. ratio_q3_q1 axis "nominal_diameter|installation_orientation": DN15 H: 80/100/125/160... hmm ratio varies within DN for H. Actually axis could be per variant. Simpler: axis "nominal_diameter|installation_orientation", values: [{condition: "DN=15, H", value: "80/100/125/160"}? No — values must be structured objects with numeric value. Could list as separate conditions: {condition: "DN=15, orientation=H, ratio", ...} — circular.

Better: ratio_q3_q1 config_level axis "nominal_diameter|installation_orientation|minimum_flowrate"? Hmm.

Actually the cleanest: the config axis IS the combination (DN, orientation, R). So define config_level entries with axis "configuration (nominal_diameter, installation_orientation, ratio_q3_over_q1)":

- minimum_flowrate_q1: conditions as above (10 entries)
- transitional_flowrate_q2: 10 entries
- ratio_q3_q1: could be derived from condition label — skip or include with values like {condition: "DN=15, orientation=H", value: "80, 100, 125, 160"} — but value must be number/range/string. Could be string "80/100/125/160". Hmm, rule 2 says formulas/symbols keep as string. A list of values shouldn't be a list-as-value per rules... "Lists of values. 25,30,50,60,75,90 (multiple Emax values) is a MODEL MATRIX". So don't put "80/100/125/160" as a single string value. Instead, I can just note ratio_q3_q1 via matrix_tables and omit config-level duplicate.

And also:
- ratio_q2_q1: 1.6 (all variants) — this is type_level: value 1.6, dimensionless.

Also matrix_tables: preserve Table 1 as matrix table(s). The example (R137) shows both matrix_tables AND model_level. Here I'll do matrix_tables with the two blocks (H and V), and use config_level for varying flow rates.

Also models: should I define model_family.models as combinations? The instruction: "model_family: include ONLY if cert covers >1 model variant". The cert covers multiple variants. I could define models as e.g. {"model_id": "SD-A DN15 H R80"} — 20 entries. That seems excessive but follows the intent. Alternatively models = SD-A, SD-AP only. Hmm.

Given DN15/DN20 and orientations create genuine variants, I think a reasonable approach: model_family.family_name = "SD-A / SD-AP" (or null), models as combination of type × DN × orientation × R. 20 models: SD-A has 10, SD-AP has 10.

Let me enumerate:

Type SD-A (and same for SD-AP):
H orientation:
1. SD-A DN15 H R80: Q3=2.5, Q1=0.03125, Q2=0.05, Q4=3.125
2. SD-A DN15 H R100: Q1=0.025, Q2=0.04
3. SD-A DN15 H R125: Q1=0.02, Q2=0.032
4. SD-A DN15 H R160: Q1=0.015625, Q2=0.025
5. SD-A DN20 H R80: Q3=4, Q1=0.05, Q2=0.08, Q4=5
6. SD-A DN20 H R100: Q1=0.04, Q2=0.064
7. SD-A DN20 H R125: Q1=0.032, Q2=0.0512
8. SD-A DN20 H R160: Q1=0.025, Q2=0.04
V orientation:
9. SD-A DN15 V R40: Q1=0.0625, Q2=0.1
10. SD-A DN20 V R40: Q1=0.1, Q2=0.16

Same ×2 for SD-AP → 20 models.

With model_level entries then: attribute × model matrix with 20 values each for q1, q2, q3, q4, ratio. That's verbose but complete. Alternatively config_level as I described with 10 conditions each is more compact and doesn't duplicate across SD-A/SD-AP since the attributes don't depend on type.

The schema allows both. Given the attributes do NOT vary by type (SD-A vs SD-AP differ only in body material), config_level with axes DN × orientation × ratio seems most faithful and compact. Then model_family.models can just be the two types? But SD-A and SD-AP are already type_designations...

I'll do: model_family with family_name null (no explicit family name) and models being the 20 configuration variants? Hmm, but then model_level values must reference those model_ids. If I use config_level instead, models can be fewer.

Decision: I'll use config_level for the flow parameters (axis: "nominal_diameter × installation_orientation × ratio_q3_over_q1" for Q1/Q2; axis "nominal_diameter" for Q3/Q4), and NOT enumerate 20 models. For model_family, include models = the two types? The rule says include only if cert covers >1 model variant. SD-A and SD-AP are type designations. The variants come from DN/orientation/R combos. I think including model_family with the 20 variant IDs is the most complete per the R137 example. But it's noisy.

Compromise: model_family.models = [{"model_id": "SD-A"}, {"model_id": "SD-AP"}] — these are the models (types) covered. And the config variations in config_level. Actually wait — the schema example for R60 shows models as {"model_id": "Emax=25t"} etc., i.e., variant descriptors. For R137, models = size variants. Here, variants = combination of type, DN, orientation, ratio.

I'll go with 20 model entries. Actually, let me reconsider: 20 entries × attributes. If I define model_level matrices referencing 20 models, each attribute list has 20 values. That's 100 value objects. Heavy but precise.

Alternatively: 10 models parameterized without type prefix (since attributes don't depend on type): "DN15-H-R80", ..., and models list notes both types share the configurations. Hmm, that conflates.

I think the cleanest given schema:
- type_designations: ["SD-A", "SD-AP"]
- model_family: family_name: null, models: 20 entries with model_id like "SD-A DN15 H R80" and attributes embedded? The models[] entries have attributes{} field! "models[]: {model_id, label, attributes{}}". So I can put per-model attributes directly in attributes{}: q3, q1, q2, q4, ratio_q3_q1, ratio_q2_q1, connection_thread, construction_length options.

That's elegant: each model carries its own attributes. Then characteristics.model_level can be omitted or minimal. But rule 4 says to populate model_level. Hmm, the R137 example populates both matrix_tables and model_level. But with 20 models, model_level lists get long.

Let me think about what a consumer would want: attribute × model matrix for querying. I'll do:

model_family.models: 20 entries with model_id and attributes (dn, orientation, ratio, q3, q1, q2, q4, connection_thread, construction_length_mm).

characteristics.type_level: shared attributes:
- mpe_upper_flow_rates_range: hmm it's conditional: ±2 at ϑ≤30°C; ±3 at ϑ>30°C. That's config_level with axis "water_temperature"? Yes:
  - attribute: mpe_upper_zone, axis: "water_temperature", values: [{condition: "ϑ ≤ 30 °C", value: -2? ...}]. MPE ±2% — value 2 with... sign. Could record value 2, unit "%", and note it's ±. Or value as string "±2"? Rules say numbers not strings. ±2 → value 2, unit "%", maybe add attribute name mpe_upper...% with tolerance. I'll record value: 2, unit "%", and the condition. Hmm, but ± matters. I could make value a range {min:-2,max:2}? That changes meaning (MPE is ±2% meaning error limits ±2%). I think value: 2 with unit "%" and attribute "maximum_permitted_error_upper_zone" plus maybe a note. There's no note field... footnote? I could add footnote-like. Simpler: value as range {min: -2, max: 2}? Actually ±2% MPE means the error must be within ±2%, so range [-2, +2] is semantically accurate. I'll use {min:-2, max:2}. Hmm, but that could be misread as MPE varies from -2 to 2. MPE is a limit pair. Range is fine.

Actually, let me keep it simpler: value: 2, unit "%", and include the ± in attribute semantics. Many extraction systems would prefer {min:-2,max:2}. I'll go with range since it captures the ±.

Hmm, wait. Let me not overthink. I'll use value: 2 and add "tolerance": "±" ... no, schema for value objects: {value, unit_symbol, unit_id, footnote_markers}. No extra keys allowed? The schema shows that shape; adding "note" might violate strictness. I'll use range {min:-2,max:2}.

- water temperature range: T30, T50 — temperature classes: T30 means 0.1–30°C, T50 means 0.1–50°C. The cert says "Water temperature range ϑ: T30, T50" with unit °C. I'll record temperature_class: value "T30, T50"? That's a list... config axis? The classes are options. I could record as water_temperature_class with value "T30/T50" string? Rule about lists of values being model matrix applies to numeric Emax. Temperature classes T30, T50 are two configuration options. I'll record as config? Or just type_level value string "T30, T50". Hmm. Values as strings allowed when not numeric. I'll do two config conditions? Overkill. I'll record type_level: water_temperature_classes: {value: "T30, T50"} — string. Actually maybe better: temperature_class with footnote... no. Keep string.

- maximum_working_pressure: 16 bar
- scale_interval: 0.00005 m³
- capacity_of_calculator: 9999.99995 m³
- mechanical_class: "M1"
- climatic_class: {min:-10, max:55} °C
- installation_orientation: H (horizontal with indication device on top) and V — footnoted. The first table row H with footnote *) "horizontal position with the indication device positioned at the top only". Second table V. So type_level: installation_orientation: {value: "H, V"}? With footnote markers ["*)"]. Or config? I'll record installation_orientation: {value: "H, V", footnote_markers: ["*)"]}. Hmm the footnote applies to H. Fine to attach to the combined value; text clarifies.

Actually footnote marker in markdown is `<sup>*</sup>)`. So marker "*")" or "*)". I'll use "*)".

- ratio_q2_q1: 1.6
- accuracy class 2 (from recommendation)
- meter position: horizontal/vertical from description.

type_level could also include: mpe_lower_zone: {min:-5,max:5} %.

config_level:
- attribute: maximum_permitted_error_upper_flow_rates_zone, axis: "water_temperature", values: [{condition: "ϑ ≤ 30 °C", value: {min:-2,max:2}, unit:"%"}, {condition: "ϑ > 30 °C", value: {min:-3,max:3}, unit:"%"}]

- attribute: minimum_flowrate_q1, axis: "nominal_diameter × installation_orientation × ratio_q3_over_q1", values: 10 entries with conditions like "DN 15, H, R 80".

- transitional_flowrate_q2: same 10.

- permanent_flowrate_q3, axis "nominal_diameter": [{condition: "DN 15", value: 2.5}, {condition: "DN 20", value: 4}]
- overload_flowrate_q4, axis "nominal_diameter": 3.125 / 5
- ratio_q3_q1, axis "nominal_diameter × installation_orientation": DN15 H: "80, 100, 125, 160"? — lists shouldn't be single values... For ratio, maybe axis "nominal_diameter × installation_orientation × minimum_flowrate"? circular again.

Alternative: axis "nominal_diameter × installation_orientation", values:
- {condition: "DN 15, H", value: "80/100/125/160"} — string of options. Rule says lists of numeric values should be matrices. But here the ratio is a design option per variant. The variant-condition already includes ratio for q1/q2. For ratio itself as attribute, I could give 8 conditions for H: {condition: "DN 15, H, Q1=0.03125", value: 80}, ... too circular.

Better: ratio_q3_q1 axis "nominal_diameter × installation_orientation" with values as multiple entries each with distinct condition combining R:
- {condition: "DN 15, H, R 80", value: 80}? Redundant.

Cleanest: give ratio per variant via model attributes (in model_family.models[].attributes) and matrix_tables, and skip config-level ratio. Or config_level ratio with axis "configuration" listing conditions "DN 15, H" → value string "80, 100, 125, 160" (as options). I'll include in matrix_tables anyway which preserves everything. I'll put ratio_q3_q1 config values as separate conditions per combination with the four R values for H as four entries {condition: "DN 15, H, R 80", value: 80}... that's silly.

Decision: I'll include ratio_q3_q1 in config_level with axis "nominal_diameter × installation_orientation" and value as string "80 / 100 / 125 / 160" for H variants — hmm violating "lists as matrix" rule. The rule specifically: "Lists of values. 25,30,50,60,75,90 (multiple Emax values) is a MODEL MATRIX — emit model_level entries, NOT a list-as-value." So I should not. OK: omit ratio from config_level; it's fully captured in matrix_tables rows and model attributes.

Now model_family. Let me decide to include models with attributes. 20 entries:

For SD-A:
- {model_id: "SD-A DN15 H R80", attributes: {dn_mm: 15, installation_orientation: "H", ratio_q3_q1: 80, permanent_flowrate_q3_m3h: 2.5, minimum_flowrate_q1_m3h: 0.03125, transitional_flowrate_q2_m3h: 0.05, overload_flowrate_q4_m3h: 3.125}}
- ... etc.

Wait, attributes{} — free-form object. Should units be embedded in key names? That's ugly but schema doesn't specify attribute structure. Alternatively attributes: {"nominal_diameter": {"value": 15, "unit_symbol": "mm"}}. The schema says attributes{} without specifying structure. I'll use structured values consistent with rule 2: each attribute key → {value, unit_symbol} objects. Hmm, that doubles size. Or simpler: attributes with unit in key like "dn_mm". I think consistent structured objects are safer per "Structured values — STRICT. Every characteristic value MUST be an object..." — that rule is about characteristics values. For model attributes, I'll use the same structured shape to be safe.

Hmm, this is getting huge. 20 models × 7 attributes × structured = large JSON but fine.

Actually, let me reconsider: maybe use 10 models with model_id including "SD-A/SD-AP" prefix? Like "SD-A/SD-AP DN15 H R80"? The table header says Type: SD-A / SD-AP — the parameters apply to both types identically. So models could be 10 configuration variants, each available as both SD-A and SD-AP. model_id: "DN15 H R80 (SD-A / SD-AP)". Hmm.

I think cleaner: models = 10, model_id like "SD-A/SD-AP DN15 H R80". Because the cert itself lists parameters jointly for "SD-A / SD-AP". And type_designations already captures both types. I'll do 10 models.

Wait, but is that confusing? A consumer matching "SD-A DN15 H R80" wouldn't find exact id. I'll add label to each model: "SD-A or SD-AP, DN 15, horizontal, R 80". Good.

Alternatively models: 20 with explicit type. I'll go with 20? Hmm. Let me weigh: The certificate: "Type: SD-A, SD-AP". Table: "Type: SD-A / SD-AP". So parameters common to both types. 20 models is more explicit and machine-friendly for exact matching. But attributes don't differ by type. I'll go with 20 for precision — no wait, that duplicates all attributes 2×.

Let me just go with 10 models with model_id "SD-A/SD-AP DN15 H R80" style. Hmm, actually...

You know, I'll do models per (DN, orientation, R) = 10, with model_id like "DN15-H-R80" and label mentioning both types. And type_designations: ["SD-A", "SD-AP"]. I think that's reasonable and I'll note in matrix_tables description.

Hmm, one more consideration — the schema example R60: models [{"model_id": "Emax=25t"}] — bare variant descriptors without type prefix. So "DN15-H-R80" style is consistent. Good.

Models:
1. DN15-H-R80: Q3 2.5, Q1 0.03125, Q2 0.05, Q4 3.125, thread G ¾B, L 110/115/130/165
2. DN15-H-R100: Q1 0.025, Q2 0.04
3. DN15-H-R125: Q1 0.02, Q2 0.032
4. DN15-H-R160: Q1 0.015625, Q2 0.025
5. DN20-H-R80: Q3 4, Q1 0.05, Q2 0.08, Q4 5, thread G 1B, L 130/165/190
6. DN20-H-R100: Q1 0.04, Q2 0.064
7. DN20-H-R125: Q1 0.032, Q2 0.0512
8. DN20-H-R160: Q1 0.025, Q2 0.04
9. DN15-V-R40: Q1 0.0625, Q2 0.1
10. DN20-V-R40: Q1 0.1, Q2 0.16

All have ratio_q2_q1 = 1.6, max working pressure 16 bar, scale interval 0.00005 m³, etc.

attributes per model: dn (15/20 mm), installation_orientation (H/V), ratio_q3_q1 (80/100/125/160/40), permanent_flowrate_q3 (m³/h), minimum_flowrate_q1, transitional_flowrate_q2, overload_flowrate_q4, connection_thread, construction_length options.

Construction length L: DN15: 110/115/130/165 mm (options); DN20: 130/165/190 mm. As attributes: {value: "110/115/130/165", unit_symbol: "mm"}? Or {value: [110,115,130,165]}? A list of options — these are alternative lengths, not a model matrix. I'll use string "110/115/130/165" with unit mm. Acceptable since they're alternative options.

Now matrix_tables: I'll create two tables:

Table "Technical parameters — horizontal installation (H)":
columns: ["parameter", "unit", "dn15_r80", ...]? Or rows per parameter. The original is transposed (parameters as rows). Better to reshape into rows = variants:

Table A (H orientation):
columns: ["nominal_diameter", "permanent_flowrate_q3", "minimum_flowrate_q1", "transitional_flowrate_q2", "overload_flowrate_q4", "ratio_q3_q1", "ratio_q2_q1"]
rows:
- {nominal_diameter: 15, q3: 2.5, q1: 0.03125, q2: 0.05, q4: 3.125, ratio_q3_q1: 80, ratio_q2_q1: 1.6}
- {nominal_diameter: 15, ..., ratio 100, q1: 0.025, q2: 0.04}
- {nominal_diameter: 15, ratio 125, q1: 0.02, q2: 0.032}
- {nominal_diameter: 15, ratio 160, q1: 0.015625, q2: 0.025}
- {nominal_diameter: 20, q3: 4, q1: 0.05, q2: 0.08, q4: 5, ratio 80}
- {nominal_diameter: 20, ratio 100, q1: 0.04, q2: 0.064}
- {nominal_diameter: 20, ratio 125, q1: 0.032, q2: 0.0512}
- {nominal_diameter: 20, ratio 160, q1: 0.025, q2: 0.04}

Table B (V orientation):
rows:
- {nominal_diameter: 15, q3: 2.5, q1: 0.0625, q2: 0.1, q4: 3.125, ratio_q3_q1: 40, ratio_q2_q1: 1.6}
- {nominal_diameter: 20, q3: 4, q1: 0.1, q2: 0.16, q4: 5, ratio 40, ratio_q2_q1: 1.6}

Plus a common parameters table? Could add matrix_table "Common technical parameters": rows parameter/unit/value:
- connection thread DN15: G ¾ B; DN20: G 1B
- construction length DN15: 110/115/130/165; DN20: 130/165/190
- water temp class T30, T50
- max working pressure 16 bar
- MPE upper ±2/±3 %, lower ±5 %
- scale interval 0.00005 m³
- calculator capacity 9999.99995 m³
- mechanical class M1
- climatic -10..+55 °C

I could capture those in type_level/config_level characteristics instead, plus keep matrix_tables for the flow matrices. Also include a "general technical parameters" matrix table to be faithful. I'll add it as a third matrix_table with rows keyed by parameter and nominal_diameter condition.
